geometry.rules: A face is a formation, shaped to its ground (the owner, 2026-09-28: no fixed box, no pit, a distinct bottom). Its anchor is the middle column of its face line; `front` is the side a player works it from (north: the player stands north and the rock runs +z; south -z; west +x; east -x); u runs along the face (+x on a north or south face, +z on a west or east face), d into the rock, d < 0 in front. The floor F is the lower median of the natural ground over the first apron row, u = -(width_max/2 + apron_margin) .. +: never lowered, so a face is walked onto, never climbed down into. The width is width_min + h32(seed, face, 1) mod (width_max - width_min + 1), half-width hw = width // 2. Column u of the face line (|u| < hw) stands back one block when h32(seed, face, 2, u) mod 3 == 0. The body: the `body_depth` cells behind the face line in each column u = -hw..hw, rows F+2 .. F+height+1, over the bottom course at F+1 (the face's `bottom` block: a contrasting rock that shows where the ore ends), and host rock from the ground up to F where the ground dips under F. The formation's top over the body is T0 = F+height+2, plus 1 where h32(seed, face, 3, u, d) mod 3 == 2; round the body, out to knoll_side beside and knoll_back behind, it is T0 + (h32(seed, face, 3, u, d) mod 3 - 1) - round(fall x (max(0, |u| - hw) + max(0, d - body_depth + 1))). A column whose natural ground is under that top is built up in host rock to it, its top cell the `cap` (the site's ground: moss, grass, snow; host rock where none); a column whose ground is at or over it is left natural, so on a slope the face is a cut and on flat ground an outcrop. No column is built up more than max_build. In front: the apron_rows rows over u = -hw - apron_margin .. hw + apron_margin, and the set-back cells, are made level with F (host rock filled under a floor block where the ground was lower, by at most max_fill; dug where it was higher, by at most max_cut), with air from F+1 to the higher of the ground and F, plus clear_above. The skin: every natural cell next to that air and at or under its column's ground becomes host rock. The bedrock (only where the site says): one cell beside, behind and under the body and its bottom course, below the ground, never in front. The ore of variant k: n = ore_min + h32(seed, face, k) mod (ore_max - ore_min + 1) body cells in the order h32(seed, face, k, x, y, z) sorts them: first visible_min on the face line at rows F+2 or F+3 with |u| <= hw - 1, then the rest at least one behind the face line and under the body's top row (tools/mines.py ore_cells). The restore puts back the whole formation (body, bottom course, rock, cap) over the resettable tag, then one variant's ore where host rock stands.

siting.why: Flight finding 2 (the owner, 2026-09-28): 'some of them arent near towns enough, like mining town someone wouldnt know its connected.' Each site's `ring` is now the nearest band round the town's centre in which a whole formation still clears every street, the plaza and every routed leg by keep_clear.road_clear, and the search adds centre_pull per block from that centre to its score, so of two legal sites the nearer to the town wins even when it costs more rock to build. The owner's recorded mix (a piece on the square, or in a house slot) is not built: a square IS the plaza and every lot touches a street, so either would put written columns inside the road_clear the owner set in finding 1. Away from the plaza wins (the owner, 2026-09-29); the square and the lot are recorded as the alternative in STONE_FACES_REDESIGN.md section 6.

keep_clear.why: No written column on a town's plan or outside its reach (tools/town_dressing.py Mask), on painted water or within 4 of a painted tree, within water_changed_reach of a column the pending water export changes (the owner, 2026-09-28: nothing built that the export would invalidate), or near another system's pieces (dressing, working Pokemon); in the Displaced City's cavern, clear of its trees, lights and tunnel (derived/cavern/plan.json, the cavern's 40_light function); faces face_gap apart; and (2026-09-28, the owner: found, not walked past) every written column road_clear from any street, the plaza and every routed leg, and each surface face's anchor inside its site's ring round the town's centre

restore.why: STONE_ECONOMY.md 5.3 and 6.2: at least 600 s (12,000 ticks) between restores of a face, checked only on approach (fill fails on an unloaded chunk, so a fixed timer would mostly fail silently): every 100 ticks, only while a player is inside the site's approach box (the faces' bounds grown by approach_margin across, approach_down below and approach_up above); the two faces of one stone at a place kept 300 s (6,000 ticks) apart. Game time and the scores are saved with the world, so a restart neither repeats nor loses a restore
restore.resettable_why: STONE_ECONOMY.md 5.4: the restore fills host rock only over this tag and guards every ore setblock with it, so a chest a player left in a box survives with its contents (it blocks one ore cell until it is moved); the hosts, what a player digs them into, torches, fluids, snow and every stone ore are reset. That `fill ... replace #tag` takes a block tag in 1.21.1 is proof P-3, not run

sites.reading: A shoulder of sea rock a minute's walk up from the light, where an estuary no river uses any more undercut the bank: water stones where the water left. The keeper will point you at it. The seam repairs the rock, not your things.

sites.reading: Grey tors standing among the tea rows at the edge of the town, a lane or two off the square: the tea houses face their walls with the polished stone, leaf out of one and the shine out of the next.

Terracotta humps the scraping left, out among the ruins but off their streets: the rock under the city's footprint is terracotta, Cobblemon's own host for the sun stone, and you chip what is exposed. The near end of the exchange.

Two seams in the cavern's walls, cut into the shell past the cavern's edge: a pale one in dripstone (Cobblemon's own host for the moon stone) and a crackling one in deepslate where the Magnemite gather. The far end of the exchange; the seam ends in bedrock, near an authored void (STONE_ECONOMY.md 6.4).
sites.road_clear_why: The owner kept the city's four sites (2026-09-28): in the cavern the wall is the view, and each face was set back 28-49 from the ring streets as a box. The formation is wider than the box, so the clearance here is 12, not the surface's 25.

sites.reading: Snow-capped outcrops on the islet just past the field station's last hut: ice stones worked out of the isle's own rock.
Dark tors and pale ones standing over the hamlet's fields, where the Tilpey outflow left the seam near the surface: dusk in the deepslate, dawn in the pale stone beside it. Late on purpose (O-3).

The town's own working, on the ground behind the pithead rather than out on the cone: the thermal face for fire and the deep seam for thunder, the second source of the most-needed stone. The Exchange stands on the pithead yard (data/traders.json mining_assayer).
